answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can place orders, with the lock lasting through a rolling pulse of activity. Rewards accrue only after counterparties confirm useful work; proven fraud burns the stake, while honest agents recover it after a delay. A sybil attacker must therefore fund every identity separately and keep capital immobilized across the horizon, making fake accounts costly even when a pearl of an account is cheap to create.
